anchor.fact: publicly refused acknowledgement for the twenty-eighth year

allowed.fact: ratnamma comes to the house and states that she was married eleven days to the appointee, who died on 14 August 1994 after a lorry collision at the Hosakere junction on his way to file the joining report.

allowed.location: the lane outside the family house
allowed.fact: ratnamma challenges mallesha in the lane to say what she is to him; he answers with a line about the fourth standard timetable and walks to the cowshed.
ratnamma produces the only print of the 16 July 1994 wedding photograph, in which mallesha stands behind the groom holding the garland; chaitra learns the two men were brothers.

allowed.location: Nerlige school, gate and assembly ground
allowed.fact: ratnamma demands in the school yard that mallesha say his own name once and she will tear up the petition; he answers with the fourth standard timetable and walks to his classroom.

A claim petition for forty-one lakh sixty thousand rupees is served at the school gate at assembly time, naming the department as first respondent and savithri as second; ratnamma privately tells chaitra she wants a paper and not the money, and gives her until the hearing on the twenty-second.
ratnamma withdraws the claim as against savithri, says so aloud in front of the lane, and is taken inside the house for the first time in twenty-eight years.

In the same corridor and in front of the same ninety witnesses, chaitra produces three documents: the seva register entry placing thammanna as payer of the 1994 funeral, the 2011 registered power of attorney in which thammanna personally identified savithri as the wife of a man dead seventeen years, and the receipt book counterfoils whose body text is in the same hand as this month's inward register entry.
thammanna is arrested in the corridor on the registered-document offence, and his name is spelled aloud twice — once into the enquiry record and once on the arrest memo.

revanna settles the ledger aloud: sale deed and mutation referred for cancellation and the four acres restored; ratnamma's arrears recommended against thammanna and not the family; shankarappa censured permanently and the school's second building block sanctioned; puttaraju suspended; mallesha dismissed, criminally referred, and the recovery reduced by the three lakh forty-five thousand six hundred rupees proved extorted; savithri says her husband's name aloud to strangers for the first time.
harsha's family return the engagement tray and chaitra refuses the match aloud in front of the corridor, in the same public form in which it was withdrawn.
basavaraj reads serial nine of the district appointment list aloud to the corridor: assistant teacher, Nerlige — chaitra, daughter of mallesha.

forbidden.fact: chaitra presents six original documents for teacher-recruitment verification and is told the file is flagged on a deceased-record cross-check.
basavaraj stamps her study certificate REJECTED in violet ink.
At chaitra's own demand basavaraj reads aloud to ninety waiting people that the man named as her father died on 14 August 1994.
savithri burns the certified copy of the birth certificate in the kitchen fire rather than answer chaitra's three questions.
harsha's family return the engagement tray at the gate without entering the house, in view of the lane.

forbidden.location: the family house, inner room, trunk under the cot
forbidden.fact: chaitra finds the 1994 appointment order in the trunk and sees that the photograph gummed to its corner is not her father's face.
mallesha refuses to look at the photograph and leaves for school before six.
thammanna collects twelve hundred rupees from the rice tin as he has on the seventh of every month since 1998, and in the same visit raises the unmutated four acres at Nerlige.
thammanna leaves the receipt book open on the step; chaitra counts 288 entries of twelve hundred rupees each, every one signed by her father in an unfamiliar hand, the earliest predating her birth.
Asked point-blank for mallesha's name after nineteen years in the next room, girija can only answer 'Master'.

A departmental staff census requires every teacher to answer to their name and give a thumb impression in front of the whole school; chaitra interrupts from the back and demands the name be read at full volume.
shankarappa reads out the name Lokanath and mallesha raises his hand and answers present, in front of four hundred children and his daughter.

mallesha states in eleven sentences that the house was mortgaged for thirty-eight thousand rupees for the marriage, that the appointee died before joining so nothing was payable, and that a block office clerk came in September 1994 and told him the date column of a joining report is written by a clerk.

chaitra names the shame she has carried since she was eight — that she told people her father was a coward for never standing for a photograph — and mallesha explains the avoidance in one sentence about newspapers reaching the block office.
chaitra opens the cloth pouch and finds that column four of her own birth certificate, registered 14 January 2000, names lokanath as her father.

inchara introduces herself and reveals she has held a photocopy of the Nerlige family tree register since 2019 and has done nothing with it while waiting for someone from that house to become angry in a government building.
chaitra files form fifteen for correction of the father's name in the birth register and says the name mallesha aloud in a government office for the first time since 1994.

thammanna states his price — the four acres mutated to his son-in-law and a resignation signed in the dead name by the fifth of next month — and enters the correction application in the inward register as received from 'daughter of Lokanath'.

chaitra intercepts revanna between the chair and the car; he orders her file reopened and directs that the reason be read out at the counter, and states that an anonymous 2019 complaint from that taluk was returned to him marked no irregularity over puttaraju's signature.
basavaraj reads the reopening order aloud to the same corridor of ninety people and addresses chaitra as madam.
The movement register shows mallesha's district service file was requisitioned at 09:20 that morning by thammanna, purpose recorded as pre-audit scrutiny.
mallesha writes a voluntary retirement letter on false medical grounds and signs it in the dead name, intending to meet thammanna's terms and clear his daughter's file.

shankarappa refuses to forward the resignation and states that he compared the joining photograph with the man in 2011, saw they were different men, locked the register and said nothing for eleven years.

Before school that morning shankarappa posted, by registered acknowledgement due from a post office outside his own village, a statement to revanna naming which man has signed the Nerlige staff attendance register since 1998 and admitting his own eleven-year silence.
thammanna rides past the gate without stopping on the seventh for the first time in twenty-four years; the audit team sat on the fifth and he handed nothing over.
seetharama produces volume four of his seva register; the entry of 16 July 1994 records the marriage, and records that the dakshine was paid by the groom's younger brother.

Under rule sixty-one revanna accepts the temple record plus two attesting statements — from the bride's uncle and from girija, who attended the 1994 marriage — and sanctions family pension to ratnamma, arrears referred to government.

Four lines below the marriage entry, the seva register records the funeral rites of 25 August 1994 — eighty fed, sixteen hundred and one rupees — with the payer's column filled in the name of thammanna, three weeks before he claims he was first deputed to the village.
puttaraju states he signed the 2019 nil report without reading it, one of sixty-one files signed that day; shankarappa admits article two orally in front of his own staff.
mallesha refuses his name three times; chaitra says it aloud from the back of the hall and girija repeats it in front of the staff; nagaraj records the name mallesha and takes the spelling.

nagaraj announces there will be a criminal reference and recovery of all pay drawn since November 1994, then asks mallesha to sign the statement in his own name; mallesha states he has not written his own name since 4 November 1994 and takes four minutes over four letters.

Sale deed number 1147 conveying the four acres by the canal is registered on the strength of the 2011 general power of attorney; no member of the family is present and none learns of it for fifteen days.
savithri states that in 2011, when prakash's chest fever needed eleven thousand rupees the house did not have, thammanna had her execute a general power of attorney she never read to the end.

thammanna's recorded statement casts him as the 2019 informant and a reluctant recipient of a bribe paid by the family for twenty-four years; he produces the receipt book counterfoils and denies the temple entry as a priest's book.
inchara hands over the recovery notice for one crore eleven lakh forty thousand rupees and the office file copy of the 2019 complaint, whose covering slip is signed by thammanna.

bible.want: To file, refile, and publicly press her claim until a numbered government record places ratnamma beside lokanath, while keeping the arrears demand alive as leverage.
bible.wound: She refuses to return as a private supplicant whose place can be denied at a gate, so she knowingly turns recognition into litigation and people into respondents. It protects her from being dismissed quietly, but costs her years, allies, and the risk of punishing people who did not erase her.
bible.voice: Her calm speech is short, flat, and formal; under pressure it expands into long accumulations of dates, sums, routes, and counted occasions. She repeats the exact number that proves she remembers. When emotion approaches, she changes the subject to chronology, paperwork, or who stood where. When frightened, her voice becomes small and she reduces everything to one concrete demand: one name, one line, one answer said back aloud.
bible.engine: Because ratnamma has no government record recognizing her marriage, every procedure sends her to another certifier, witness, or office. She cannot distinguish an ordinary missing record from a refusal serving someone else's interests, so she treats every silence as another procedural obstacle. To obtain signatures and guidance, she carries petitions for other unrecorded people in exchange; every favor creates another deadline, obligation, rival claim, or official to confront, turning her personal case into an expanding shadow network of people the state cannot easily see.

offscreen_ledger.window: between the season opening and b013
offscreen_ledger.what: ratnamma sorts twenty-eight years of rejection slips and postal acknowledgments by date, queues at government counters, dictates fresh representations at a typing stall, trades help with other petitioners for stamp paper and witness leads, and pays an advocate to calculate an arrears claim large enough to force a hearing.

ratnamma has careful copies made from the wedding photograph, visits former guests seeking attesting statements, sends registered demands to several offices, helps two other widows prepare replies in return for introductions to clerks, and instructs her advocate to draft a claim against both the department and savithri so it cannot be left unanswered in a cupboard.

ratnamma collects proof that the petition was served, refuses an informal cash compromise, prepares a signed instruction allowing savithri to be removed from the claim, and drafts a declaration clearing her that can be read where the lane will hear it.

ratnamma obtains a certified copy of the withdrawal, rebuilds her document bundles after repeated handling, records the names of everyone willing to attest to the wedding, rehearses her own evidence by date and number, and repays petition favors by accompanying other claimants to counters where they are afraid to speak alone.

bible.reframe: The mainline is about a family trapped inside a stolen public identity; ratnamma's serial is about an unrecorded widow building a parallel civic system of favors, testimony, and public shame to compel the state to admit that her eleven-day marriage existed.
bible.pitch: With one fading wedding photograph and twenty-eight years of refusals, an unregistered widow turns every government counter into a courtroom.

episode.title: The Fourth Standard Answer
episode.logline: After twenty-eight years without recognition, Ratnamma confronts her late husband’s brother before the entire lane—and turns his humiliating refusal into testimony.
episode.script:
SFX: A metal gate rattles. Bicycle bells pass. A dog barks twice, and low voices gather along the lane.

RATNAMMA: Is this Mallesha’s house?

CHAITRA: Who are you?

RATNAMMA: Call him first.

SAVITHRI: He has not come from school.

RATNAMMA: Then I will wait outside. I have waited inside offices. Outside offices. Under one staircase from ten in the morning until the clerk locked the upper floor at six. This lane has shade.

KEMPANNA: What work do you have with the master?

RATNAMMA: Work that began twenty-eight years ago.

SAVITHRI: Speak quietly. There is no need for the whole lane.

RATNAMMA: There is every need. Quietly, I have received no answer.

CHAITRA: Answer to what?

RATNAMMA: My name is Ratnamma. I was married to Lokanath for eleven days. Lokanath was the appointee. On 14 August 1994, he died after a lorry collision at Hosakere junction. He was on his way to file the joining report.

SFX: A steel water pot stops scraping. Two children quit whispering.

KEMPANNA: Eleven days?

RATNAMMA: Eleven. Not ten. Not twelve. Eleven days with a husband and twenty-eight years being asked to bring somebody who remembers it.

CHAITRA: Why have you come here?

RATNAMMA: Because Mallesha remembers.

SAVITHRI: You cannot arrive at a house and say such things.

RATNAMMA: I arrived at a gate. I stated my name, my husband’s name, the number of days and the date of death. Which thing should have been said elsewhere?

SFX: A bicycle stand strikes stone at the end of the lane.

KEMPANNA: Master has come.

RATNAMMA: Good. Nobody move.

SFX: A cow pulls against its rope. Slow footsteps approach, then stop beside the gate.

MALLESHA: Why are these people standing here?

SAVITHRI: This woman came asking for you.

RATNAMMA: This woman has a name.

MALLESHA: I have school work.

RATNAMMA: Twenty-eight years and you still cannot walk through your own gate when I am sitting in it.

MALLESHA: Move away from the gate.

RATNAMMA: (louder, to the lane) Master! You want me to go? Say my name and I will go. Not Ratnamma. Say who I am to you. Say it once, in the lane, and I will get up and I will never come to this gate again.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

RATNAMMA: One sentence. These people are listening. Your wife is listening. This young woman is listening. Say who I am to you.

MALLESHA: The fourth standard timetable has to be written.

SFX: Footsteps cross the yard without hurry. A wooden cowshed latch lifts. The gate remains shut.

KEMPANNA: He answered you with a timetable.

SAVITHRI: Enough, Kempanna.

KEMPANNA: She asked what she was to him. He said fourth standard timetable. We all heard it.

RATNAMMA: Yes. All of you heard it.

CHAITRA: Why did he go to the cowshed?

RATNAMMA: Ask him.

CHAITRA: I am asking you.

RATNAMMA: I do not manufacture answers for men who are standing close enough to speak.

SFX: A cow bell shakes behind the wall.

RATNAMMA: Mallesha! I am still at the gate. Your timetable did not move me.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

KEMPANNA: Twenty-eight years, and she gets a school timetable in front of the lane.

RATNAMMA: Do not laugh.

KEMPANNA: I was not laughing at you.

RATNAMMA: Everyone says that after a woman has been made ashamed in public. I am ashamed. Let that also be spoken plainly. But I am still sitting here.

SFX: A cloth bag opens. Papers crackle. A pencil scratches against the back of an envelope.

RATNAMMA: What time is it?

CHAITRA: Four twenty-five.

RATNAMMA: Say it again.

CHAITRA: It is four twenty-five.

RATNAMMA: Four twenty-five. In the lane outside Mallesha’s house. Present: Savithri, Chaitra, Kempanna and the people at the wall. Question asked: who is Ratnamma to Mallesha? Answer given: the fourth standard timetable has to be written.

SAVITHRI: What are you writing?

RATNAMMA: What happened.

SAVITHRI: On an old envelope?

RATNAMMA: The government has rejected cleaner paper than this.

KEMPANNA: Write my name. I heard him.

RATNAMMA: Spell it.

KEMPANNA: K-E-M-P-A-N-N-A.

RATNAMMA: Chaitra, will you sign as a witness?

CHAITRA: I do not know you.

RATNAMMA: You know the question. You know the answer. Sign only for those two things.

CHAITRA: What will you do with it?

RATNAMMA: Put it behind the other unanswered papers. Then, when somebody asks whether I came here, I will not have to beg this lane to remember me.

SAVITHRI: Do not involve her.

RATNAMMA: She is already standing here. I did not put her ears on her head.

CHAITRA: Give me the pencil.

SFX: Pencil scratches. A cow stamps inside the shed.

RATNAMMA: Full name.

CHAITRA: Why?

RATNAMMA: Because half a name gives an office room to escape through.

SFX: The pencil scratches again.

CHAITRA: There. But I still do not understand why he should answer you.

RATNAMMA: I asked for one relationship said aloud. He chose a timetable. Now I will show you why that answer matters.

SFX: The cloth bag opens again. Paper bundles shift. A stiff photograph catches against an envelope.

RATNAMMA: Do not touch the surface. Hold the white edge.

CHAITRA: This is a wedding photograph.

RATNAMMA: The only print. Sixteenth of July, 1994.

SAVITHRI: Ratnamma—

RATNAMMA: No. He had his answer. Now I have mine.

CHAITRA: Which one is Lokanath?

RATNAMMA: The groom.

CHAITRA: And the bride is you.

RATNAMMA: Yes.

CHAITRA: Who is standing behind him?

RATNAMMA: The tall man with his sleeves folded. Look at his hands.

CHAITRA: He is holding the garland.

RATNAMMA: He is holding it behind the groom so it does not touch the ground.

CHAITRA: That is my father.

RATNAMMA: That is Mallesha.

CHAITRA: Why is he standing behind your husband?

RATNAMMA: Lokanath was his elder brother.
